CODER TASK T5.c1

CHANGE
Right now `storage.dumps` never writes `desk.holds`, so every hold is lost on save and load. Fix that in two files.
1. `shelf/holds.py`: add `Hold.to_dict()`, which returns `{"isbn", "member_id", "placed": format_date(placed)}`. Add the classmethod `Hold.from_dict(d)`, which does the reverse and turns `placed` back into a date with `parse_date`. Add `HoldQueue.restore(holds)`, which appends each Hold to `self._queues[hold.isbn]` in the order given. If a hold has the same ISBN and member as one already queued (or one added earlier in the same call), raise `ValueError` with the same message `place` uses.
2. `shelf/storage.py`: `dumps` adds a top-level `"holds"` key: `[h.to_dict() for h in desk.holds.all()]`. `loads` calls `desk.holds.restore(Hold.from_dict(d) for d in data.get("holds", []))` once the desk exists. A document with no `"holds"` key loads with no holds.

INTERFACES
- `shelf/holds.py`: `Hold` (dataclass: `isbn: str`, `member_id: str`, `placed: date`), `HoldQueue.place`, `HoldQueue.all()` (sorted by ISBN, oldest first within each ISBN), and the new `Hold.to_dict`, `Hold.from_dict` and `HoldQueue.restore`.
- `shelf/dates.py` (read only): `format_date(d)` returns an ISO string; `parse_date(text)` returns a date.
- `shelf/storage.py`: `dumps(catalog, members, desk)`, `loads(text, clock=None)` and `FORMAT = 2`.
- `shelf/loans.py` (read only): `LoanDesk.holds` is a `HoldQueue`, created in `__init__`.

CONSTRAINTS
- Edit only `shelf/holds.py` and `shelf/storage.py`. `FORMAT` stays 2. Do not change the format of any existing key.
- `dumps` keeps `json.dumps(..., indent=2, sort_keys=True)`, so dumps → loads → dumps must still give identical text.
- Import `format_date` and `parse_date` from `.dates`. Do not write your own date handling.
- Do not change behaviour of `place`, `cancel`, `queue`, `pop` or `all`.

BUILD/TEST
`python -m unittest discover -s tests`. Green means every test passes, with no errors and no failures.

DONE WHEN
- The test suite is green.
- A desk with holds on two ISBNs survives dumps → loads with the same `holds.all()` (ISBN, member and placed date, in the same order), and dumps again to identical text.
- Loading JSON with the `"holds"` key removed gives an empty `holds.all()`.
- `restore` with a duplicate (same ISBN and member) raises `ValueError`.
Check the last three with a quick inline Python run and record the output in the log. Do not add a test file.
